names.note: Read out of saint.gr's page for 19 Μαΐου, whose head line for him is «Αγιος Παυλος ο Ιερομαρτυς» and whose list names him «Παύλος Μιχαήλοβιτς Κρασνοκούτσκιυ», with the rank words left off.

floruit.note: The one year the source gives him, and it is not a death year: saint.gr's line in its list of the Kharkov new martyrs, «Ο Άγιος Ιερομάρτυς Παύλος Μιχαήλοβιτς Κρασνοκούτσκιυ, ο οποίος φυλακίσθηκε το 1930.» — imprisoned in 1930. The list says of the company that they died between 1937 and 1941, but says it of all but one and does not say which, so no death year is recorded here.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Νεομάρτυρες εν Σλομπόντσκαγια Ουκρανίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The company is enumerated — twenty-seven men named one by one, with patronymics, birthplaces and the months of their deaths — so it is twenty-seven folders and not one, by docs/CORPUS.md §10.1. Nothing in the corpus answers to any of these surnames: a grep of `saints/` for all twenty-seven returned nothing, and no folder mentions Kharkov except `meletius-of-kharkov`, a bishop of the eighteen-hundreds. His own head line reads «Αγιος Παυλος ο Ιερομαρτυς», and his sentence in the page's list is quoted whole in the life. His is the one sentence in the list that gives no birth and no death: it says only that he was imprisoned in 1930, and his head line carries no years at all. So there is no `dates` object for him, and the page's calling him Ιερομάρτυς is the only ground for the type.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
